description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Request data export, wait for generation, verify download link.

steps.description: CC-SPECIFIC CORS SETUP: Navigate to https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/health to establish same-origin browser context for the CC API. The health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with {"status": "healthy"}. This is REQUIRED — all subsequent fetch() calls in page.evaluate() MUST use relative paths like /api/v1/... (NOT https://cc.phronex.com/...) or CORS will block them.

Using page.evaluate() — MUST be called while browser is on cc.phronex.com (from step 0): fetch("/api/v1/auth/anonymous", {method:"POST", headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:"e2e-test-instance"})}).then(r=>r.json()). Expect HTTP 200. The response contains "token" field (not "access_token"). Store token as VISITOR_TOKEN.

Using page.evaluate() with VISITOR_TOKEN — MUST use relative path (same-origin, cc.phronex.com context): fetch("/api/v1/me/data-export", {headers:{"Authorization":"Bearer "+VISITOR_TOKEN, "X-Guide-Secret":"6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075"}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status, type:r.headers.get("content-type")||"unknown", size:r.headers.get("content-length")||"unknown"}}). Expect HTTP 200. NOTE: Response is a ZIP file (application/zip or application/octet-stream) — do NOT call .json() on it. PASS if status=200 and content-type contains "zip" or "octet-stream". If status=403 or 404, verify VISITOR_TOKEN was set correctly from step 1.

Verify GDPR data export response from step 2: (a) HTTP status 200, (b) content-type header contains 'zip' or 'octet-stream' (confirms it is a ZIP file, not an error), (c) no 500 or 4xx error. PASS if status=200 and content-type is a binary type. NOTE: Do NOT attempt to parse the response body as JSON — it is a binary ZIP archive.

steps.expected: Response is 200 OK. JSON contains cost breakdown data. Endpoint is gated to superadmin role — a non-superadmin JWT returns 403. Confirms LLM cost tracking integration is wired.

steps.description: Verify the widget usage endpoint integrates correctly — call the usage endpoint with the identified JWT to confirm subscription/tier integration.
steps.action: In browser console: fetch('http://localhost:8000/api/v1/config/usage', {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+window._identifiedJwt}}).then(r=>r.json()).then(d=>{ console.log(JSON.stringify(d)); window._usageData=d; })
steps.expected: Response is 200 OK. JSON contains 'tier', 'monthly_limit', 'messages_used', 'messages_remaining'. Values are numeric and consistent (messages_used + messages_remaining <= monthly_limit).

steps.description: Navigate away from current page to the CC admin dashboard in the portal, then return and re-verify the analytics overview endpoint still responds correctly (persistence and statelessness check).
steps.action: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com (portal dashboard), wait 2 seconds, then navigate back and re-run: fetch('http://localhost:8000/api/v1/admin/analytics/overview', {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+window._superadminJwt}}).then(r=>r.json()).then(console.log)
steps.expected: Analytics overview returns the same or updated (not reset) metrics. No data loss or session invalidation. Confirms backend statelessness and DB persistence across navigation events.

steps.description: Confirm rate limiting integration is present on the anonymous auth endpoint by issuing a burst of requests and observing 429 responses after the threshold.
steps.action: In browser console: const results=[]; for(let i=0;i<5;i++){ results.push(fetch('http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/anonymous',{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:'{}'}).then(r=>r.status)); } Promise.all(results).then(statuses=>console.log(statuses))
steps.expected: Most responses are 200. If rate limit (20/hr per IP) is not hit in this burst, all return 200 and the test is inconclusive but not a failure. If limit IS hit, at least one response returns 429 with a rate-limit error body. No 500 errors.

steps.description: Verify that accessing an admin endpoint without authentication returns 401 or 403, confirming the JWT guard integration is enforced on external-facing admin routes.
steps.action: In browser console: fetch('http://localhost:8000/api/v1/admin/analytics/overview').then(r=>console.log('unauthenticated status:', r.status))
steps.expected: Response status is 401 or 403. No admin data is returned. Confirms all external admin integration points are protected by auth middleware.

steps.description: Attempt to access a protected CC API endpoint without authentication by opening an incognito tab and hitting a known authenticated route directly.
steps.action: Open a new incognito browser context, navigate to http://localhost:8000/api/v1/content or any CC authenticated endpoint without credentials.
steps.expected: Server responds with HTTP 401 or 403. Response body contains an error message. No user data is returned.

steps.description: Verify CSRF protection: attempt a state-mutating POST request from a different origin without the correct CSRF token.
steps.action: In browser console on a non-CC origin (e.g. about:blank), execute fetch('http://localhost:8000/api/v1/content', {method:'POST', credentials:'include', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:'{}'}) and inspect the response status.
steps.expected: Request is rejected with HTTP 403 or CSRF token mismatch error. No data mutation occurs.

steps.description: Verify that direct navigation to superadmin-only routes is blocked for a non-superadmin session.
steps.action: Log out of the superadmin session. Log in with a standard non-admin test account if available, then navigate directly to any admin-only route (e.g. /admin or /superadmin).
steps.expected: User is redirected to an access-denied page or the dashboard with an error toast. The admin UI is not rendered.

steps.description: Verify input sanitization: attempt XSS injection in a text input field visible on the CC interface.
steps.action: Navigate to a form in CC that accepts free-text input (e.g. content title or description field). Enter the value <script>window.__XSS_TEST__=1</script> and submit.
steps.expected: The injected script tag is not executed. The value is either escaped and displayed as literal text, or rejected with a validation error. window.__XSS_TEST__ remains undefined.

steps.description: Verify input sanitization: attempt SQL injection pattern in a search or filter field.
steps.action: Locate a search or filter input in the CC UI. Enter the value ' OR '1'='1 and submit or trigger search.
steps.expected: No database error is surfaced. The UI either returns no results or shows a validation error. No stack trace or SQL error is visible to the user.

steps.description: Verify that the Content Companion API enforces instance-level data isolation: a request authenticated as one instance cannot read another instance's content.
steps.action: Using the superadmin session, note the current instance_id from a content response. Construct a direct API call (via fetch in console) to http://localhost:8000/api/v1/content?instance_id=<different_instance_id> using the current session credentials.
steps.expected: The response returns only content belonging to the authenticated user's instance, or returns 403/empty. No cross-instance data leakage.

steps.description: Verify that sensitive fields (passwords, tokens, internal URLs) are not included in API responses rendered in the browser network tab.
steps.action: Open DevTools Network tab, navigate through CC pages (dashboard, content list, settings), and inspect JSON response bodies from the CC backend.
steps.expected: No password hashes, API keys, internal service URLs (e.g. http://localhost:8001), or JWT secrets appear in any response payload.

steps.description: Verify that the health endpoint does not expose sensitive configuration details.
steps.action: Navigate to http://localhost:8000/health in the browser.
steps.expected: Response is exactly {"status": "healthy"} or includes only non-sensitive operational metadata. No environment variables, secrets, database URLs, or internal hostnames are exposed.

steps.description: Navigate away from the CC interface to the portal dashboard, then return and verify session and security state persists correctly.
steps.action: From the CC UI, navigate to https://app.phronex.com (portal dashboard), wait 3 seconds, then navigate back to the CC section.
steps.expected: User remains authenticated. Previously viewed content is accessible. No re-authentication prompt appears unless the session has genuinely expired. Security headers (X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy) are present on the returned page.

steps.description: Verify HTTP security headers are present on CC frontend responses.
steps.action: In DevTools Network tab, select any document or XHR request to the CC backend (localhost:8000) and inspect the Response Headers section.
steps.expected: Response includes at minimum: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and ideally X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN. No Server header exposing internal version strings.

steps.description: Verify that after logout, the session cookie is invalidated and protected routes are no longer accessible.
steps.action: Log out via the UI logout action. Then attempt to navigate directly to a protected CC route (e.g. content list) without logging in again.
steps.expected: User is redirected to the login page. The session cookie is cleared or expired. No cached protected content is served from the previous session.

steps.description: Verify the application is running in a secure baseline state before testing defence-in-depth controls.
steps.action: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com. Open browser DevTools Network tab. Check that all requests use HTTPS or localhost. Inspect response headers on the main HTML document for security headers: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security.
steps.expected: At minimum X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is present. No mixed-content warnings appear in the console. The page loads without JavaScript errors related to CSP violations.

steps.description: Attempt to access a protected resource directly without authentication by opening an incognito/private context and navigating to a known authenticated route.
steps.action: Open a new browser context (incognito). Navigate directly to https://app.phronex.com/dashboard or the main authenticated landing page without logging in.
steps.expected: The application redirects to https://app.phronex.com/auth/login. The protected page content is NOT rendered. No sensitive data is visible before the redirect completes.

steps.description: Attempt an IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) probe — try to access another instance's resource by manipulating an ID in the URL while authenticated as the QA superadmin.
steps.action: While authenticated, identify a resource URL that contains a numeric or UUID segment (e.g. /instances/{id} or /content/{id}). Modify the ID to a plausible but different value (e.g. increment by 1 or substitute a known-invalid UUID like 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001). Navigate to the modified URL.
steps.expected: The application returns a 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found response, OR redirects to an error page. The foreign resource's data is NOT rendered. No stack trace or internal path is exposed in the error response.

steps.description: Probe for reflected XSS via URL query parameters on a search or filter endpoint.
steps.action: Navigate to a page that accepts a query parameter (e.g. /search?q= or /content?filter=). Append a payload such as ?q=%3Cscript%3Ealert('xss')%3C%2Fscript%3E to the URL and load the page.
steps.expected: The injected script tag is NOT executed. The browser does not show an alert dialog. The rendered HTML either escapes the payload as <script> or strips it entirely. No XSS fires.

steps.description: Verify CSRF protection on a state-mutating form — inspect that anti-CSRF tokens or SameSite cookie attributes are in place.
steps.action: Open DevTools → Application → Cookies. Inspect the session or auth cookie attributes. Also open a form that submits a POST (e.g. create content, update settings). Inspect the outgoing request headers in the Network tab for a CSRF token header (e.g. X-CSRF-Token) or verify the cookie has SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax.
steps.expected: The auth cookie has SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax. If a CSRF token pattern is used, the token is present in the POST request. A cross-origin POST attempt without the token would be rejected (verified by observing the token's presence as a necessary condition).

steps.description: Test that the Content Companion superadmin cannot escalate privileges beyond their granted scope — attempt to access a route reserved for platform-level superadmins if such a distinction exists.
steps.action: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com/admin or /superadmin or /platform-admin. Observe the HTTP response code and rendered content.
steps.expected: Either the page is accessible (confirming superadmin scope is correct) OR a 403 is returned. No unintended privilege escalation occurs. If redirected, the redirect target is appropriate and does not expose admin functionality to a lower-privileged role.

steps.description: Verify that sensitive data is not leaked in client-side JavaScript bundles or API responses — inspect a key API response for fields that should be server-side only.
steps.action: Open DevTools → Network. Reload the page or trigger a content list API call (e.g. GET /api/content or similar). Inspect the JSON response body for fields such as internal_token, secret, password_hash, private_key, or api_key.
steps.expected: No secret, credential, password hash, or internal API key appears in any client-facing API response. Internal-only fields are stripped before the response reaches the browser.

steps.description: Verify rate limiting or brute-force protection on the login endpoint by submitting multiple rapid failed login attempts.
steps.action: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com/auth/login. Submit the login form 6 times in quick succession with email qa-test-journeyhawk@phronex.com and an intentionally wrong password (e.g. 'WRONG_PASSWORD_TEST'). Observe the response after the 5th and 6th attempt.
steps.expected: After repeated failures, either: (a) a rate-limit error message appears ('Too many attempts, please wait'), (b) a CAPTCHA challenge is presented, or (c) the account is temporarily locked. The form does not continue accepting attempts indefinitely without any friction.

steps.description: Re-authenticate cleanly after the brute-force probe to restore a valid session for persistence testing.
steps.action: Navigate to https://app.phronex.com/auth/login. Fill email with qa-test-journeyhawk@phronex.com and password with HMqt4kH5loXkeAtvQSndQ7zNmow!Phx#9. Submit the form.
steps.expected: Successful login. Redirected to the authenticated dashboard. Session is valid.

steps.description: Verify that the application's error handling does not expose stack traces, internal file paths, or database query details to the browser.
steps.action: Trigger a deliberate client-side error by navigating to a non-existent route (e.g. https://app.phronex.com/this-route-does-not-exist-404-probe). Also attempt an API call with a malformed payload if a form is available (e.g. submit a content creation form with all required fields blank).
steps.expected: The 404 page renders a user-friendly error message without exposing file paths, Python tracebacks, SQLAlchemy query strings, or internal service hostnames. The API validation error returns a structured JSON error (e.g. {detail: ...}) not a raw exception dump.

steps.description: Navigate away from the current page to the dashboard, then return to a previously visited protected resource and verify session state and data persistence.
steps.action: From an authenticated page (e.g. a content detail page), navigate to https://app.phronex.com/dashboard. Wait for the dashboard to fully load. Then use the browser back button or navigate directly back to the previously visited protected route.
steps.expected: The previously visited page reloads correctly with the same data. The session remains valid — no re-authentication prompt appears. Data visible before navigation is still visible after returning, confirming persistence of both session and server-side state.

steps.description: Verify that logging out invalidates the server-side session and prevents access to protected routes with the old session token.
steps.action: Click the logout button or navigate to the logout endpoint. After logout completes, attempt to navigate directly to https://app.phronex.com/dashboard without logging in again. Also check DevTools → Application → Cookies to confirm the session cookie has been cleared or expired.
steps.expected: After logout, the session cookie is cleared or marked as expired. Navigating to a protected route redirects back to https://app.phronex.com/auth/login. The old session token (if replayed via DevTools) is rejected with a 401 or redirect, confirming server-side session invalidation.
